description: Rebuilding Roads to Maximize Resilience is a case study listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by Colorado Department of Natural Resources Water Conservation Board; Colorado Department of Transportation; Colorado Parks and Wildlife. After an extremely heavy rain destroyed almost 500 miles of roadway in Colorado, the state is redesigning some roadways and the streams they follow to make the roads more resilient to future floods. Coverage: Colorado (2015). The toolkit gives Colorado as the location, 2015 as the year. The listed link gives the documented application. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the cited source documents and the outcomes reported were not checked, and no model or dataset used was verified. It can support comparison with similar adaptation projects and planning precedents. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.

outcomes: In September 2013, a slow-moving cold front stalled over Colorado and mixed with warm, humid airflows from the south—the result was a devastating deluge across Colorado’s Front Range. The severe rain, which lasted more than a week, caused catastrophic flooding and damage, including 10 fatalities, numerous injuries, and more than $535 million in state highway and local roadway damage. The massive floods destroyed or damaged nearly 500 miles of public roads and temporarily closed 39 different roadways.
